answer: Proof-of-personhood seals resist Sybil attacks: each identity must present a zero-knowledge credential, issued once per real person by independent issuers, proving uniqueness without revealing who they are — a jade seal that cannot be copied. A nebula of fake aliases collapses, because one person can mint only one seal, no matter how many keys they generate. Identities without a seal sit in a lagoon of zero weight: they may watch but never vote or earn, so buying a thousand fakes means buying a thousand real people.
